question: Can the input-dependent action of a neural network be represented as local source and drain impulse responses, extending classical filter echoes into a general and visually interpretable neural-network framework?

key_findings.claim: A fixed-input ReLU convolutional network can be written as an input-dependent linear operator whose columns and rows act as source and drain echoes.
key_findings.evidence: For a bias-free DnCNN residual branch, the paper freezes the input-induced ReLU masks and composes convolution and diagonal activation matrices into P(f), giving the denoiser u=(I-P(f))f and state matrix S(f)=I-P(f).

anchors.section: IV-A Simplified DnCNN without Biases and Batch Normalization

key_findings.claim: Homogeneous coordinates extend the echo construction to biases, inference-time batch normalization, and affine network maps.
key_findings.evidence: The paper augments inputs with a constant coordinate, embeds each affine layer in an extended matrix, and derives u=(I-P)f-d; the additive vector d is treated as a separate bias echo.

key_findings.claim: For differentiable networks the proposed state matrix coincides with the local Jacobian, so saliency-style drain echoes and adversarial source echoes are special cases.
key_findings.evidence: The affine local form u=S(f)f+b is matched to a Taylor linearization; output-to-input partial derivatives form rows and input-to-output effects form columns. The authors argue their layerwise construction also handles nondifferentiable points without differentiating through the network.

anchors.section: V Neural Echoes for General Networks

key_findings.claim: In one synthetic denoising example, a DnCNN echo visually reflects both spatial and gray-value similarity while achieving lower error than a tuned bilateral filter.
key_findings.evidence: On a 32-by-32 binary-pattern image with Gaussian noise sigma 15, the rendered source echoes show spatially local and tonally selective weights; reported MSE is 2.08 for DnCNN versus 15.46 for the bilateral filter optimized at spatial sigma 12.5 and tonal sigma 43.

method.core_idea: At one input, rewrite every network component as a data-dependent matrix or affine matrix and interpret the composed input-output operator using the source/drain echo language of signal processing.
method.mechanism: Convolutions become sparse matrices, ReLUs become diagonal masks evaluated on the original forward pass, and biases plus batch-normalization offsets are represented in homogeneous coordinates. Applying the composed matrix to impulses yields source echoes; reverse transposed application yields drain echoes without materializing the full matrix.
assumptions: The forward-pass state is fixed while an echo is propagated, so data-dependent gates and weights describe a local rather than global operator.
Each component can be represented by an input-conditioned linear or affine action at the evaluated input.
A visualized row or column of this operator is a meaningful explanation of network behavior.
The single binary-image DnCNN case is sufficient as a conceptual demonstration, not as broad empirical validation.

techniques.role: Expresses a nonlinear network at a fixed input as an input-conditioned state-transition matrix.
Absorbs biases and normalization offsets into extended affine matrices while retaining a compositional form.
Computes selected matrix columns or rows through ordinary and transposed layer operations instead of storing an enormous dense matrix.
Separates how one input location propagates to outputs from which inputs contribute to one output location.

evaluations.setting: One 17-layer DnCNN trained for 60 epochs on binarized 40-by-40 patches, tested on one 32-by-32 synthetic binary image with Gaussian noise sigma 15
evaluations.metric: Mean squared error and qualitative source-echo structure
evaluations.result: DnCNN MSE 2.08; its rendered echo is spatially local and appears more tonally selective
evaluations.baseline: Bilateral filter with MSE-optimized spatial sigma 12.5 and tonal sigma 43, MSE 15.46

limitations: The authors explicitly present only a proof of concept, not a comprehensive empirical evaluation.
The experiment uses one simplistic synthetic binary image and one DnCNN, despite broad claims covering classifiers, recurrent networks, and transformers.
The full state matrix can be prohibitively large; selected echoes can be propagated implicitly, but comprehensive source-and-drain coverage still scales with input and output dimension.

Reviewer inference: an exact fixed-input affine decomposition does not itself establish that the displayed weights are causally faithful under finite interventions, especially when the input crosses activation regions.
Reviewer inference: the experiment optimizes the bilateral baseline on the test image and reports no seed variation, natural-image evaluation, perturbation test, or human interpretability study.
failure_modes: An echo can change discontinuously when a small perturbation changes an activation gate or other input-dependent layer state.
Signed, unnormalized echo weights can be visually hard to interpret and can hide cancellation across paths.
A local matrix may reproduce the output at one input while giving misleading counterfactual effects for perturbations outside that local region.
Attention, normalization, routing, or discrete components may require bespoke state freezing; an informal matrix analogy can conceal omitted derivative terms.
Visually plausible edge or tonal patterns may persist after parameter randomization, so appearance alone cannot demonstrate model dependence.
reusable_insights: Expose both columns and rows of an input-output operator when sender and receiver questions are scientifically different.
Use homogeneous coordinates to keep affine components composable and to make bias contributions auditable rather than silently dropping them.
Compute only requested operator slices through matrix-vector and transpose-vector products; explanation tooling need not construct a dense Jacobian.
Compare learned local kernels with explicit model-based kernels to turn an explanation into a concrete hypothesis for improving the hand-designed model.
Pair visualization with randomization, perturbation, and reconstruction tests before interpreting a local operator as an explanation.
open_questions: Do neural echoes pass model-parameter and label-randomization sanity checks?
How stable are echoes across nearby inputs, activation-boundary crossings, layers, and independently trained seeds?
Can the construction be implemented faithfully and efficiently for layer normalization, softmax attention, mixture-of-experts routing, and nondifferentiable modules?
Do echo-derived hypotheses improve explicit filters on natural-image benchmarks rather than one synthetic case?
Which quantitative faithfulness, completeness, or causal-intervention property should a neural echo satisfy?

competitive_landscape.title: Full-Gradient Representation for Neural Network Visualization
competitive_landscape.difference: FullGrad decomposes outputs into input and per-neuron bias sensitivities and evaluates completeness with perturbation and retraining tests; neural echoes instead expose full sender/receiver operator slices, extend the filter-kernel metaphor, and claim nondifferentiable support but provide much lighter validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Integrated Gradients assigns feature credit along a baseline-to-input path and satisfies sensitivity and implementation invariance; neural echoes describe a local input-output transfer matrix at one state and do not establish these attribution axioms.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Important Features Through Propagating Activation Differences
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepLIFT propagates prediction differences from a reference activation and provides feature contribution scores in one backward pass; neural echoes propagate fixed-state impulses in forward or transpose direction and preserve a spatial filter interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
competitive_landscape.difference: Sanity Checks demonstrates that visually appealing explanations can be independent of learned parameters or labels and supplies randomization tests; neural echoes offer a new visualization but do not run those essential dependence tests.

novelty_assessment: The authors' novelty claim is a signal-processing generalization of source and drain filter echoes to neural networks, including affine terms and purportedly nondifferentiable architectures. Reviewer inference: the sender/receiver filter vocabulary and constructive DnCNN derivation are distinctive, but the differentiable case substantially overlaps Jacobian and full-gradient representations. Broad architectural generality is argued algebraically rather than demonstrated, and explanatory faithfulness remains unvalidated.
reviewer_notes: Read all seven pages and checked the rendered page containing Figure 2, equations, and the experiment. The visual comparison supports the limited claim that the two echoes look spatially and tonally structured; it cannot support causal faithfulness. Quantitative results are author-reported. Competitor titles, records, and current arXiv revisions were checked against arXiv or official PMLR pages on 2026-08-23.
